items.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I had this chance to go down and jam and play with Scott Hamilton... So I got all the records that Duke told me to get... and then I would join Scott’s band... we only did six gigs before Scott left for New York

ctx.x: Well why don’t you fill me in, because there’s probably all sorts that I don’t know about.

Well the immediate few that come to mind are my contemporaries in Geneva, in years probably ‘72 to ‘74, Michael Hashim, the alto saxophonist, and Chris Flory the guitarist, also with Scott Hamilton. His original home is Geneva also. And a drummer by the name of John Ellis in New York. Those are just Genevans. And I’ve become more aware of other upstaters like Mel Lewis and Lonnie Smith the organist — they’re Buffalo guys. and then of course all the other Italian upstate guys, the Joe Romanos and the Scott LaFaros.
Right. Did you get into Rochester much as a kid, fairly close, to hear any music in there? You wound up going to Eastman, right?
